morgan (Springboard): hey team — starting ~07:00 UTC we see a lot of 429s across our prod app. baseline ~200 RPM but getting short spikes to ~1.2k RPM every minute causing many failed jobs. example error: "429 Rate limit exceeded". any quick ideas?

sara (support): sorry about that — can you paste a sample request-id + response headers? are you using streaming or non-streaming requests? did you deploy anything this morning?

morgan (Springboard): request-id: rq_9f8e2b1c. headers we get back:
```
HTTP/2 429
x-request-id: rq_9f8e2b1c
x-rate-limit-policy: rpm=600;tpm=10000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 30
```
We're not streaming, just short synchronous HTTP calls from our worker fleet. we also have a retry worker that requeues failed tasks.

sara (support): thanks — that header shows you're hitting the per-minute RPM bucket (600). spikes to 1.2k would definitely exhaust the window. couple quick checks: are your retries exponential / jittered? are you opening many concurrent connections (HTTP/2 streams or parallel clients)? any cron or heartbeat that aligns to minute boundaries?

morgan (Springboard): our retry logic is simple: immediate retry up to 3 times with fixed backoff 5s. we do have a minute-aligned heartbeat across pods (legacy).

ops-bot: alert: HIGH_429_RATE detected for tenant springboard-prod at 3180001240 — 429s/sec > threshold :warning:

rahul (eng-sre): looping in eng-sre — @morgan can you do a quick curl to capture raw headers so we can verify the Retry-After behavior? example:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -D - https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```
that will print response headers. also if you can share a short tail of your worker logs showing the retry timestamps it helps identify fan-out.

morgan (Springboard): pasted tail of worker timeline: many failures at 07:00:00 then a surge of immediate retries at 07:00:05 across ~80 pods, so the retry floods the same minute bucket. sample lines:
```
2026-03-17T07:00:00Z job=gen id=abc status=429 req=rq_9f8e2b1c
2026-03-17T07:00:05Z job=gen id=abc retry=1
2026-03-17T07:00:05Z job=gen id=def retry=1
... many similar across hosts ...
```

sara (support): that pattern is a classic retry thundering herd. immediate retries align with the minute window and push you over the RPM. short-term mitigations: lower client concurrency, add jittered exponential backoff, stagger heartbeats off-minute, or temporarily request a soft quota increase. long-term: implement per-process leaky-bucket client side smoothing or use Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput.

alex (platform): we can open a temporary soft-burst window for 10 minutes while you roll a fix. please open a ticket with the tenant id + sample times + request-id. i'll add that to SUP-3245. also if this is recurring we recommend switching heavy workloads to Dedicated to avoid tenant-level contention.

morgan (Springboard): ok we'll patch retry behavior immediately (add jitter and backoff). can you enable the soft window now?

sara (support): done — created SUP-3245 and enabled a 10m soft-burst allowance at 07:10 UTC. eng-sre (rahul) assigned. :thumbsup:

rahul (eng-sre): I'll try to reproduce with a controlled replay from your request traces. if it's the queue replayer we may recommend configuring the replayer to cap concurrency and apply randomized backoff. quick JS example for jittered retry:
```
async function retry(fn, attempts=5) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn() } catch (e) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 1000;
      const wait = Math.min(30000, Math.pow(2,i)*1000 + jitter);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries')
}
```
this avoids immediate simultaneous retries. also cap concurrent workers to 5 while you validate.

morgan (Springboard): rolling hotfix now to add jitter + cap concurrency. we'll monitor. thanks all.

sara (support): i'll keep the soft-burst active until 07:20 then revert unless you ask otherwise. i'll post followup once SUP-3245 has the quota outcome.

morgan (Springboard): update at 07:15 — after hotfix we see 429s drop to near zero and service recovered. will follow up with root cause PR to avoid minute-aligned heartbeats. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

rahul (eng-sre): leaving a checklist for the handoff: 1) confirm job replayer caps concurrency 2) remove minute-aligned heartbeat 3) migrate long-running batched jobs to use chunked requests + client-side smoothing 4) consider Dedicated/reserved capacity for steady high-throughput workloads.

sara (support): closing the immediate escalation on this thread, keeping SUP-3245 open for quota followup and recommended customer actions.

morgan (Springboard): appreciated — will send the PR and inform when done.
